newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China sells Japan JV golf club cars for tax fine.
newsitem.headline: China sells Japan JV golf club cars for tax fine.

text.p: Chinese authorities have auctioned off nine cars owned by a Japanese joint venture golf club in Shenzhen after it ignored repeated orders to pay outstanding taxes and fines, a club official said on Wednesday.

The taxation bureau of Shenzhen, the southern boomtown bordering Hong Kong, raised 2.2 million yuan ($265,060) at the auction of the vehicles, including two Lexus cars, belonging to the Honichi Golf Leisure Club, the official said.
One other car was withdrawn unsold, she told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.

The authorities have also frozen 13 million yuan in bank savings since Honichi, a venture between Shenzhen Bao Heng (Group) Co Ltd and a Japanese investor, failed to pay 95.3 million yuan in taxes and fines or respond to the allegations.
Officials declined to name the Japanese partner.
Representatives of the Japanese side have been quoted by a Hong Kong newspaper as saying there was no need to pay tax to China under the Sino-Japanese Double-Taxation Prevention Treaty.
Tax officials are likely to confiscate Honichi's other assets, including the entire golf club, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times quoted tax authorities as saying.
Officials at the golf club said the Japanese counterpart had refused them access to financial records of 977 million yuan in membership fees and deposits between 1988 and 1996.
"We are very angry towards the Japanese," the club official said, adding they may terminate the contract.
Another club official has said the Japanese side should be responsible for the tax because they handled the membership sign-ups, which totalled 3,343, the majority of them Japanese.
"The Japanese are threatening to fight a court battle and take the case to the Beijing government," the official said.
But business is continuing as usual so far for the Honichi course.
"We have 10 less cars, but golfers are still enjoying the fine summer breeze," the official said.
